text:
lara: Hey folks — we need a new GPU node pool in us-west3 for a latency-sensitive inference batch (customer-facing). Target: H100, ~24 nodes initially, multi-AZ, support burst to 40 nodes. Prefer preemptible for cost but need graceful eviction and quick fallback to dedicated. Can we sketch sizing + autoscaler policy?

tom: Agree H100 makes sense for perf. A few things to watch: ENI/IP per node in us-west3, regional quota for H100s, and pod density if we use DRA/MTU for networking. If preemptible, set a fast fallback route to a10g reserved pool. :thinking_face:

rishi: What are expected P50/P95 latencies? That affects whether we can tolerate cold starts on fallback. Also batch size distribution — if small tokens, higher QPS -> prefer more smaller nodes.

lara: P50 ~35ms, P95 ~120ms for current model (seq=1024). Most requests are single-turn. We want to keep P95 under 200ms even during preemptible evictions.

maya: For autoscaler, propose mixed-instance node pool: 70% H100-preemptible, 30% H100-on-demand (or reserved). Use CA with scale down delay 15m, expander: prioritized. Add annotation to use kube-scheduler topologySpread for AZ balance.

tom: Regarding ENI/IP: us-west3's default /20 subnets might run out at high node counts. We should request subnet expansion or use VPC CNI with IP masquerade and secondary ranges. Also check PodENI limits for h100 machine type.

lara: I'll open a subnet request if needed. For quotas, can someone file a quota increase for GPUs in us-west3? We need 40 H100s total (initial 24 + headroom).

quota-bot: Quota request submitted: project=redwood-inference, region=us-west3, resource=H100_GPUS, requested=40. Request ID: Q-2026-3317. Status: pending.

rishi: If quota is pending, we should prepare an interim plan: spin up a10g reserved pool in us-west2 as a fallback. Performance diff ~1.3x slower for some models but still within SLOs for degrade. Also consider quantized model variant for preemptible nodes to reduce memory footprint.

maya: +1 on quantized fallback. We can use nodeSelector + tolerations to prefer H100 nodes and fall back to a10g with taints. Keep rollout using a canary of 3 nodes.

tom: For eviction handling: add a DaemonSet that detects GCP preemption notice and drains pods with a 30s gracefulPeriod to push work to KV cache. Also enable pod disruption budgets: minAvailable=80%.

lara: Example nodepool config I was thinking: 
```yaml
apiVersion: autoscaling/v1
kind: NodePool (managed)
metadata:
  name: edge-h100-mix
spec:
  machineType: n1-h100
  preemptible: true
  minSize: 12
  maxSize: 40
  autoscaler:
    scaleDownDelay: 900s
    expander: prioritized
  taints:
    - key: "dedicated"
      value: "h100"
      effect: "NoSchedule"
  labels:
    pool: "edge-h100"
```
Adjust to GKE resource names as needed.

maya: That looks good. We'll need to set maxSurge=0 for upgrades to avoid transient capacity spikes causing IP exhaustion. Also add nodeAffinity to spread across three AZs.

tom: Cost check: H100 on-demand ~ $X/hr, preemptible ~30% of on-demand. 40 nodes sustained would be expensive; recommend autoscaler aggressive downscaling at off-peak (02:00-06:00 UTC) via schedule.

lara: Noted. I'll add scheduled scaling policy for nights. Also queueing backpressure in the API to avoid sudden spike scaling.

rishi: One more: ensure kernel boot times & container image warmup — use a small warm pool (3 warmed nodes) with cached model artifacts via init container. That reduces cold-start tail.

maya: I'll draft Terraform/GKE patch and a rollout playbook (canary, metrics to watch: P95 latency, GPU util, pod evictions, CA activity).

lara: Thanks — I'll wait for quota approval then trigger infra change. Tagging @quota-bot for updates. :thumbsup:
